text:
Nikita Kucherov asked the Lightning for a trade on Oct. 30 and told them he won't re-sign, saying (per NHL.com) it was about "poor communication and respect" rather than money. Julien BriseBois answered that Tampa has "unequivocally" no intention of trading him. Kucherov had passed Steven Stamkos as the franchise's all-time leading scorer six days before the request. On Saturday he scored the overtime winner against Minnesota. Whatever is broken off the ice, it isn't showing on it.

The Lightning are 11-3-2, have won three straight on 61 percent of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and take 56 percent at even strength for the season. This isn't a team riding luck: goals and chances line up almost exactly. Our simulations give Tampa a 93 percent playoff chance and a coin flip for the Atlantic.

The supporting story is depth and stability elsewhere. The Zemgus Girgensons, Pontus Holmberg and Ilya Mikheyev line has outscored teams 8-3, Charle-Edouard D'Astous has 10 points in his last ten, and Andrei Vasilevskiy's agent has indicated he intends to finish his career in Tampa. Brandon Hagel took a public jab at Dylan Larkin, which tells you how the room wants this framed: Kucherov is still playing. The question for the next three months is whether a team this good keeps him for a run or cashes him in.
headline: Kucherov wants out, and Tampa keeps winning anyway
